Style · public

STYLE-PUBLIC — the public document style

STYLE for documents that leave the building. Copy the head of this file into any document; the semantic rule and the colour rule in its comment travel with it. Below is a specimen of every element the style covers.

A second-level heading

Body text. Dark ink on white, one serif column, forty-six ems wide, with room to breathe. Inline code sits in the monospace face at slightly under the body size, so a path or an identifier does not tower over the sentence around it. A date is written 2026-09-26.

A third-level heading

For a division inside a section: the size of the body text, set in italic.

A blockquote, for a statement set apart from the argument around it.

An ordinary list, and beneath it the tighter ladder variant, for lists read as a sequence of rungs rather than as prose:

  • an ordinary list item
  • another
  1. a ladder item, spaced tighter
  2. another
  3. a third

Tables, for data with two axes

A table claims that its rows are comparable down each column. Where that is not true of the content, what is wanted is a definition list.

a header cellset as a label
a body cellruled by hairlines, top-aligned, so a long cell beside a short one still reads
code in a cellthe monospace face carries into cells unchanged

Definition lists, for a term and its description

a term
its description, with the term set as a label to match a table's header cell
another term
one axis, not two — nothing here is comparable to anything else down a column

Preformatted blocks

Code and commands are a pre wrapping a code element; a bare pre is for preformatted text that is not code.

a preformatted block of code: monospace, set off by a rule,
and scrolling sideways rather than wrapping, so a long command
line stays one line and stays copyable

Mathematics

Mathematics is written in LaTeX in the source and compiled to MathML when the document is built, so the browser typesets it natively and it stays text. Inline, it sits in the sentence: a sequence x of length N has the ambiguity function A(τ,ν). Displayed, it stands apart:

A(τ,ν)=∑n=0N−1x[n]x∗[n+τ]e−2πiνn/N

Figures, for an actual image

A figure holds an image and its caption. It is unframed, centred and given room. The caption, centred beneath it, begins with the figure's label, says what the image is, and says where it came from.

A figure that compares several things fills them with the pastels, in order, and names each in a legend above the image:

A figure that singles out one thing gives it the accent, labels it, and leaves the rest in grey:

A raster image, made of pixels, is an img whose source is a data URI. Its caption names its resolution, because pixels are all it has:

A paragraph in the meta class: smaller, in the label face, for the line under a title that says what a document is, and for a closing note on provenance.
